LESSON: FRACTIONS

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: MATHEMATICS
Strand: Numbers
Topic 1.6: Fractions
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 6

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Fractions, part of Numbers in Grade 4 MATHEMATICS.

Key inquiry question: When can you usefractions in real life? 2. 2. How can yourepresent fractions?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. discuss the top (numerator) and bottom (denominator) numbers in a fraction and share with others,

2. illustrate, in groups, fractions as part of whole or part of a group,

3. illustrate, in pairs/groups, fractions as part of a whole or part of a group using cut- outs, counters or clock face,

4. work out, in groups, proper, improper and mixed fractions as part of a whole or as part of a group using paper cut-outs or counters,

5. discuss, in groups, changing ofimproper fractions to mixed fractions, 1. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. discuss the top (numerator) and bottom (denominator) numbers in a fraction and share with others,
2. illustrate, in groups, fractions as part of whole or part of a group,
3. illustrate, in pairs/groups, fractions as part of a whole or part of a group using cut- outs, counters or clock face,
4. work out, in groups, proper, improper and mixed fractions as part of a whole or as part of a group using paper cut-outs or counters,
5. discuss, in groups, changing ofimproper fractions to mixed fractions, 1. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Fractions together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Self-efficacy: Learner confidently illustrates fractions as part of a whole or part of a group using cut-outs,

counters or clock face.

Values:
Responsibility: Learner shares roles while illustrating proper, improper and mixed fractions as part of a whole

or as part of a group using paper cut-outs or counters.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Peer Education: Learner assists others to change mixed fractions to improper fractions.
